The FILE-SCOPE AFTER-A-COMMA position is BUILT AND RUN by gcc, clang AND mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 -- 3-of-3, every reference that speaks `__attribute__` at all. The MEMBER AFTER-A-COMMA position is a minority-of-one: clang BUILDS, RUNS, AND LANDS THE ALIGNMENT AT THE SINK (a static asserting `&g.b % 16 == 0` and `offsetof(b) % 16 == 0` at RUN TIME returns 42), while gcc, mingw-w64 gcc and MSVC (in its own `__declspec(align(N))` spelling, C2143) refuse -- and under `DSS = (gcc union clang union MSVC) union ISO C`, the union over what WORKS, one working reference makes the construct REQUIRED. gcc's refusal is member-list-LOCAL, not positional: it BUILDS AND RUNS the identical spelling at file scope. $$$ THE BINDING IS PER-DECLARATOR, AND A TWO-DECLARATOR SUBJECT CANNOT SHOW IT -- WHICH IS WHY EVERY SUBJECT HERE HAS THREE. With only `a` and `b`, `char a, __attr__ b;` gives a@0 b@16 sizeof 32 whether the attribute binds to `b` alone or to the whole declaration; the candidates coincide and the probe passes either way. MEASURED 2026-09-07 with three: clang gives a=0 b=16 **c=17** sizeof 32, and the file-scope twin puts `fc` at `&fb + 1` on gcc AND clang. Declaration grain would have put `c` at 32 and sizeof at 48 -- a SILENT WRONG LAYOUT from a rule that parses and runs. $ THE LEADING POSITION IS THE CONTRAST AND IS RETAINED AS A CONTROL: it IS per-declaration (a=0 b=16 c=32 sizeof 48 on both references), it was already shipped, and keeping it in the same program is what makes the other numbers attributable to POSITION rather than to the scan. The TRAILING-on-the-last-declarator and undecorated controls are here for the same reason. $ THE UNION HALF is exercised too: `unionField` is a separate config row and therefore a separate omission. $ NO RESIDUE IS CLAIMED FOR THE GNU SPELLING: all three refused positions now parse and bind.
